news.title: ‘Oddball’ test lets us glimpse how monkeys see the world
paras: Do they see the world in the same way we do? To find out, neuroscientists in India used an “oddball” test to compare visual performances between people and macaques.

They found that, although the different species scored similarly on many aspects of perception, there were two intriguing differences: the monkeys were less phased by images being flipped upside down and they seemed far more focused on fine details. There have been previous attempts to compare human and monkey vision, but the tests often require extensive training, says S. Arun at the Indian Institute of Science in Bengaluru.

She told us, “I was lucky to have contact with Hayley Goodrick who runs the Djagala education program and she is a brilliant organiser as well as teacher so she made it easy to organise the day.”

sport.title: Why Daniil Medvedev is now one of the favourites to win the ATP Finals this year
paras: Although it is yet to be officially confirmed, Daniil Medvedev is now all but qualified for this year’s ATP Finals. It will mark his seventh participation in this prestigious end-of-year event in eight years, which is a testament to his longevity at the apex of the sport.

Having won the tournament in the past, the 30-year-old knows exactly what it takes to secure this unique title when faced against the best players in the world. And, there’s cause to believe that Daniil Medvedev can accomplish this feat again later this year.

sport.title: Greg Rusedski has theory over why Novak Djokovic is really pushing to qualify for the ATP Finals this year
paras: Novak Djokovic has set his sights on qualifying for the ATP Finals this year. Djokovic has played a limited schedule in 2026, with the 39-year-old only playing seven tournaments up to and including the US Open .

However, since then Djokovic has played more tournaments and stated his goal to qualify for the ATP Finals . Some have been surprised by this goal of Djokovic’s, particularly as he withdrew from the ATP Finals in 2024 and 2025. Djokovic has some work to do if he is to qualify for the ATP Finals this year, but former US Open finalist Greg Rusedski thinks he knows the real reason why this is such a goal for the Serbian.

sport.title: ‘Good But Not My Best’ – Carlos Alcaraz Seeks Consistency In Bid To Regain Top Form
paras: Carlos Alcaraz has plenty of positives to build on since returning to the Tour, but admits he still has work to do to reach his desired level. The seven-time Grand Slam champion missed almost five months of the Tour earlier this season due to a right wrist injury.

He started his comeback with a run to the quarter-finals of the US Open, where he was beaten in a five-set thriller by Ben Shelton. Alcaraz went on to win the Japan Open by dropping two sets in five matches played. However, he then suffered a shock third round loss at the Shanghai Masters to Zizou Bergs.

paras: Novak Djokovic is set to compete in the Basel Open for the first time since 2011. Djokovic, who is competing for an ATP Finals spot alongside the likes of Rafael Jodar and Frances Tiafoe, has been handed a difficult draw in the Swiss city .

The Serbian superstar, a 24-time major champion and Olympic gold medallist, will play Frenchman Ugo Humbert in the first round. Humbert, the world number 38, is widely recognised as one of the best indoor hard-court players on the ATP Tour . Djokovic and Humbert have played each other just once before – what was the result on that occasion?

paras: This is a WTA 500 event, but it has no bearing on the upcoming WTA Finals and the race to Indian Wells. That competition is over, with the WTA formally announcing the qualification of all eight singles players in early November.

The Pan Pacific Open therefore becomes a simple tournament where players are just trying to build their ranking for the start of the 2027 season and earn some prize money. A 500-point tournament offers the chance to make a major gain in the rankings. It’s a lot more than a WTA 250.

sport.title: Every match Venus Williams has won this year after advancing in Guangzhou Open doubles
paras: Venus Williams and Janice Tjen emerged victorious from their first-round match at the Guangzhou Open on Monday. Williams and Tjen defeated Ekaterine Gorgodse and Kimberley Zimmermann 6-0, 7-5 in the Chinese city and will now play either Lyudmyla Kichenok and Makoto Ninomiya or second seeds Jesika Maleckova and Miriam Skoch in the second round.

The American seven-time major singles champion will compete against Lilli Tagger in the singles event on Tuesday. Williams has achieved some impressive doubles results on the circuit throughout the 2026 campaign, including in Washington and Germany.
